description: DROP TABLE and CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE wired through the deferred-apply write set. When a table is dropped or replaced AFTER the same transaction has buffered INSERT/UPDATE/DELETEs against it, those buffered writes must be discarded: otherwise COMMIT tries to flush them to storage that no longer exists and fails with Failed to commit transaction (cause: Table storage does not exist), and a drop-then-recreate of the same name in ONE transaction would resurrect the pre-drop rows in the new table. The trigger in practice is a stored procedure - the whole CALL is one deferred transaction - that seeds a scratch or temporary table and DROPs it before returning, a very common test-proc cleanup shape, which crashed at commit before the fix. Converted 1:1 from transaction/DropTableDeferredApplyTest (now retired); the Java built its own engine with transaction.deferredApply=true and called setAutoCommit(false), both of which the testkit backend supplies through the default engine plus an explicit BEGIN.

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE TEMPORARY TABLE scratch (a INTEGER)
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS s

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE publish() RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ DECLARE n INTEGER; BEGIN CREATE OR REPLACE TEMPORARY TABLE s.expected (a INTEGER); INSERT INTO s.expected VALUES (1), (2), (3); n := (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s.expected); INSERT INTO keep VALUES (:n); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS s.expected; RETURN 'ok'; END $$
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS s

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE churn() RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN CREATE OR REPLACE TEMPORARY TABLE s.tmp (a INTEGER); INSERT INTO s.tmp VALUES (10), (20); DROP TABLE IF EXISTS s.tmp; CREATE OR REPLACE TEMPORARY TABLE s.tmp (a INTEGER); INSERT INTO s.tmp VALUES (99); RETURN 'ok'; END $$
